summary: Measured on the same 29 features as the other banks in the Belgian set, ING's current-account pack pages sit clearly with the traditional banks (position score 0.18), and their signature is volume rather than clarity: more figures and percentages, more persuasion techniques and more student targeting than peers, but far fewer calls to action and no comparison table at all. ING's offer is rated clearer than peers while its overall clarity score sits slightly below the peer mean. No performance data exists in this project and five of thirteen rubric features were unscored at capture, so every recommendation below is a hypothesis for ING to test, not a proven cause.

recommendations.title: Add a comparison table to the current-account pages
recommendations.finding: No ING page in the measured set includes a comparison table, against a peer mean of 0.44, one of ING's two largest negative gaps at about -0.9 SD.
recommendations.recommendation: Add a compact comparison table on the current-account pack page that lines the packs up side by side on price, included services and conditions, and place it directly above the main call to action.

recommendations.title: Increase the number of calls to action
recommendations.finding: ING shows 3.0 calls to action per page against a peer mean of 14.72, a gap of about -1.0 SD, and it is one of the three features that most distinguishes ING from the market.
recommendations.recommendation: Add repeated, clearly worded calls to action at each decision point - after the offer summary, after the comparison table and at the foot of the page - all pointing to the same opening flow rather than introducing new destinations.

recommendations.title: Build out the student and young-audience page
recommendations.finding: Targeting of students or young people is ING's largest signature gap, at 1.0 against a peer mean of 0.22 (about +1.5 SD), though this feature is model-assisted and should be read as a direction rather than a firm measurement.
recommendations.recommendation: Give the jeunes page its own offer framing, proof points and call to action instead of reusing generic current-account copy, and link it prominently from the main current-account page.

recommendations.title: Shorten the current-account page
recommendations.finding: ING's current-account pages run to about 9,465 px against a peer mean of about 6,611 px (about +0.7 SD), so the page carries substantially more scroll than its peers.
recommendations.recommendation: Cut the page back towards peer length by merging or removing supporting sections, and move secondary detail such as fee schedules and legal text behind a disclosure rather than keeping all of it in the main scroll.

recommendations.title: Reduce the opening image
recommendations.finding: The opening image takes about 0.53 of the page at ING against a peer mean of about 0.29 (about +0.9 SD), and it is ING's largest positive layout gap.
recommendations.recommendation: Shrink the hero image and spend the freed space on the offer statement and a call to action, keeping the overlaid text-on-image arrangement ING already uses rather than returning to text beside picture.

recommendations.title: Pair every figure with a plain-language payoff
recommendations.finding: ING quotes 25.5 figures or percentages per page against a peer mean of 12.44 (about +1.3 SD), yet its clarity score of 4.5 sits below the peer mean of 4.8, so the highest number volume in the set is not producing the highest clarity.
recommendations.recommendation: For each numeric claim on the current-account and savings pages add one short sentence saying what the number means for the reader, and drop any figure that is not used in the decision itself.

recommendations.title: Carry ING's strongest persuasion techniques onto the pages that lack them
recommendations.finding: ING uses 3.5 persuasion techniques per page against a peer mean of 2.0 (about +2.1 SD), a rubric-based judgement, while its advantage on offer clarity is narrower (5.0 against 4.4).
recommendations.recommendation: Take the two or three persuasion techniques that recur on ING's strongest current-account page and apply them consistently to the savings, term-account and youth pages, keeping the meaning identical across the French and Dutch versions.

recommendations.title: Stop treating animation as a differentiator
recommendations.finding: ING carries 1.0 animated elements per page against a peer mean of 0.67, but the deck claim that ING is the only traditional bank using animation is not supported - KBC, Crelan, Belfius and Vdk all score above zero. The claim that ING no longer places text next to picture is supported: its most common layout is overlaid.
recommendations.recommendation: Keep animation as a supporting detail and keep the overlaid text-on-image layout, but do not build the page's argument on motion; put that effort into the offer statement and the calls to action instead.

recommendations.title: Have the current-account pack page ready before the campaign window
recommendations.finding: ING search interest for its current-account terms shows a sustained trend for the French term on 2026-08-30 and 2026-09-06 and an isolated spike for the Dutch term on 2026-09-06, with sustained trends continuing to 2026-09-13. Those dates sit inside the 'Level up your banking' repositioning window, whose matched campaigns follow by 1 to 8 days. Any link between that attention and a page change is a hypothesis to verify, not evidence.
recommendations.recommendation: Finalise the compte-courant pack page and its calls to action before the campaign window opens - offer wording aligned with the pack names used in the campaign - rather than updating the page after attention has already peaked.
recommendations.market_context: ING current-account terms moved on 2026-08-30, 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-13 - one isolated spike and repeated sustained trends - within the 'Level up your banking' campaign window.

recommendations.title: Prioritise the savings page in the same window
recommendations.finding: Search interest for ING savings shows sustained trends on two consecutive dates, 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-13, putting savings attention alongside current-account attention in the same window. Whether this reflects the campaign or ordinary seasonality is unverified: the 2026-09-06 match is flagged as seasonally confounded, the 2026-09-13 one is not.
recommendations.recommendation: Bring the comptes-epargne page to the same level of readiness as the current-account page for that window - offer statement, figures and a call to action - and have the compte-a-terme page ready as the follow-on destination for visitors who want a fixed term.
recommendations.market_context: ING savings search interest showed sustained-trend anomalies on 2026-09-06 and 2026-09-13, the second not flagged as seasonally confounded.

recommendations.title: Schedule current-account page refreshes ahead of spring and summer
recommendations.finding: Current-account search terms for KBC, a bank covered by the trends data, show isolated spikes clustered between March and August: 2026-03-22 at 27, 2026-05-17 at 19, 2026-07-26 at 25, 2025-08-31 at 27 and 2025-03-16 at 21. No claim is made for banks without trends data, and whether this competitor attention affects ING at all is a hypothesis to verify.
recommendations.recommendation: Plan ING's current-account page reviews and any offer refresh so the page is at its strongest entering those spring and summer windows, rather than refreshing after the attention has passed.
recommendations.market_context: KBC current-account term anomalies cluster between March and August across 2025 and 2026, with values between 19 and 27.
